subject: business-studies
title: Porter's Five Forces
welcome_lead: Five forces decide whether an industry is attractive.
meta_desc: A-Level External Environment: Porter's Five Forces of industry analysis.
final_note: Profitability is mostly about industry structure, not management heroics.

concepts.def: Intensity of competition among existing firms.
Threat from potential competitors entering the market.
Threat from products meeting the same need differently.
Obstacles that deter new entrants - capital cost, brand, regulation.

walkthroughs.body_html: Porter argues five competitive forces shape industry profitability - high rivalry, low barriers, strong buyers, strong suppliers or close substitutes all compress margins.
High barriers to entry protect incumbents: large capital requirements, patents, brand loyalty, network effects. Low barriers - like online retail in some niches - invite constant new competition.
When a small number of large buyers dominate (supermarkets vs farmers), buyer power is high. When a single supplier holds a unique input (rare-earth metals), supplier power dictates terms.
